beats.narration_en: Why is this machine swallowing a concrete wall?
It's moving the whole wall over by one lane, while traffic keeps flowing.
The wall is a chain of concrete blocks, pinned together like a bike chain.
Each block weighs about fifteen hundred pounds.
Wheels under the machine grab the T-shaped top of every block.
Then an S-shaped track lifts the chain and slides it sideways, twelve feet.
The blocks drop back down in a new line, still locked together.
In the morning, the busy side gets an extra lane. At night, it zips back.
That's why some highway walls change sides every day.
